surface: SeizureFrequency mentions with FrequencyChange in {Frequent, Infrequent}
verdict: MAGNITUDE LABELS ARE GENUINE (1/17 = 5.9% mislabeled, < 30% threshold; robust to ambiguous handling: upper bound 3/19 = 15.8% still < 30%). The conflation is by design per the annotation guideline; the deconflation probe's residual direction gap (+0.0226) is a pure model gap, not a gold artifact.

co_annotation_cross_tab.note: Letters carrying both a magnitude label and a direction label on different seizure types
co_annotation_cross_tab.finding: All co-annotation magnitude labels classify as GENUINE_MAGNITUDE (the annotator used the direction vocab elsewhere, so the magnitude label is deliberate). The one MISLABELED_DIRECTION row (EA0049 GTCS) is on a letter where the annotator also used Infrequent (absence) and Frequent (myoclonic) genuinely.

special_cases.EA0049_GTCS: The single MISLABELED_DIRECTION row. Text: 'Although the generalised tonic clonic seizures were infrequent at first they are now happening frequently' — an explicit before/after change the annotator labeled Frequent (capturing the current magnitude, not the change). A clearer label would be Increased.
special_cases.EA0022_EA0059_well_controlled: The two AMBIGUOUS rows. Both use 'well controlled' mapped to Infrequent per guideline List 11 L877-L879. 'Well controlled' sits at the boundary of magnitude (low rate) and direction (has come under control); neither reading decisively dominates.

rows.rationale: 'very frequent myoclonic jerks' — absolute-rate descriptor, no change construction.
'frequently gets myoclonic jerks' — absolute-rate descriptor; the change construction in the next sentence is about GTCS (a separate annotation).
'were infrequent at first they are now happening frequently' — explicit before/after change; should be Increased.
'continue fairly frequent, 2-3 per day' — absolute-rate descriptor; 'continue' = steady state.

'frequent drops and absences throughout the day' — rate descriptor for the flare-up days; the deterioration context ('begun to slip') is in the prior sentence about overall control, not the annotated type.
'still having fairly frequent seizures' — 'still' = continuity, absolute rate.
'still seems to be getting fairly frequent seizures' — continuity + absolute rate.
'still having fairly frequent seizures' — same as row 7, continuity + absolute rate.
'continues to get frequent seizures' — 'continues' = continuity, absolute rate.
'relatively frequent ... in the last few years' — rate over a window; the improvement ('seizure frequency has improved') is captured by a separate Decreased annotation on a different mention.
'frequent focal dyscognitive seizures in clusters ... 10-15 over 2 days' — absolute-rate descriptor.
Near-identical to EA0169 — 'frequent focal dyscognitive seizures in clusters' — absolute rate.
'infrequent ... having around two in the year' — absolute-rate descriptor (low rate).
'seizures seems to be well controlled on lamotrigine' — 'well controlled' sits at the boundary of magnitude (low rate) and direction (has come under control via treatment); neither reading dominates.
'Occasional absences' in the structured frequency header — absolute-rate descriptor.
'Occasional absences' — absolute rate; same letter carries a separate Decreased annotation on a different type.
'seizures are also well controlled' — same boundary case as EA0022.
'Infrequent focal seizures' in the Diagnosis line — diagnostic rate descriptor.
'longstanding infrequent' — 'longstanding' explicitly denies a change framing; absolute low rate.
